es: Comprobar si el relato de una entrevista es fiel a las preguntas originales y detectar cuándo omite, exagera o distorsiona.

vocabulary.es: citar mal, citar de forma inexacta
exagerar, dar más importancia de la debida

teaching.en: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even when the words change, because it is the intention that has to survive.
teaching.es: Un informe fiel conserva el sentido de la pregunta original, aunque cambien las palabras, porque lo que tiene que sobrevivir es la intención.
teaching.explanationEs: Fiel no es copiar: es conservar el sentido. Original es la pregunta tal como se formuló.
segments: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even when
the words change, because it is the intention that has to survive.
teaching.audioText: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even when the words change, because it is the intention that has to survive.

teaching.en: If the panel only asked for an example, saying that they chose to challenge his answer would distort what really happened.
teaching.es: Si el comité solo pidió un ejemplo, decir que decidió cuestionar su respuesta distorsionaría lo que realmente ocurrió.
teaching.explanationEs: Challenge es poner en duda; pedir un ejemplo no lo es. Distort cambia el sentido.
segments: If the panel only asked for an example, saying that they
chose to challenge his answer would distort what really happened.
teaching.audioText: If the panel only asked for an example, saying that they chose to challenge his answer would distort what really happened.

teaching.en: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked whether he could work on Saturdays, but only in the morning, and leaving that out changes the question.
teaching.es: No omitas la condición: el comité preguntó si podía trabajar los sábados, pero solo por la mañana, y dejar eso fuera cambia la pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: Omit: dejar fuera un dato; aquí la condición only in the morning cambia la pregunta.
segments: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked whether he could work on
Saturdays, but only in the morning, and leaving that out changes the question.
teaching.audioText: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked whether he could work on Saturdays, but only in the morning, and leaving that out changes the question.

teaching.en: To say that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate the situation, and to claim that they were furious would overstate it even further.
teaching.es: Decir que el comité exigió una respuesta exageraría la situación, y afirmar que estaban furiosos la exageraría todavía más.
teaching.explanationEs: Exaggerate y overstate suben el grado: convierten una pregunta en una exigencia o un enfado.
segments: To say that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate the situation,
and to claim that they were furious would overstate it even further.
teaching.audioText: To say that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate the situation, and to claim that they were furious would overstate it even further.

teaching.en: Adding details that nobody mentioned is a way to embellish a story, and quoting half a sentence to change its point is a way to misquote the speaker.
teaching.es: Añadir detalles que nadie mencionó es una forma de adornar una historia, y citar media frase para cambiar su sentido es una forma de citar mal a quien habla.
teaching.explanationEs: Embellish añade detalles inventados; misquote altera lo que alguien dijo realmente.
segments: Adding details that nobody mentioned is a way to embellish a story, and quoting
half a sentence to change its point is a way to misquote the speaker.
teaching.audioText: Adding details that nobody mentioned is a way to embellish a story, and quoting half a sentence to change its point is a way to misquote the speaker.

teaching.en: An accurate report chooses its verb with care: the panel may ask, enquire or press, and each verb implies a different degree of insistence, so never quote a remark out of context.
teaching.es: Un informe preciso elige con cuidado el verbo: el comité puede preguntar, consultar o insistir, y cada verbo implica un grado distinto, así que nunca cites un comentario fuera de contexto.
teaching.explanationEs: Ask es neutro; enquire about introduce un tema; press añade insistencia. Out of context: sin lo que lo rodeaba.
segments: An accurate report chooses its verb with care: the panel may ask, enquire or press, and
each verb implies a different degree of insistence, so never quote a remark out of context.
teaching.audioText: An accurate report chooses its verb with care: the panel may ask, enquire or press, and each verb implies a different degree of insistence, so never quote a remark out of context.

prompt.es: ¿Es fiel este informe a la pregunta original? Elige la valoración correcta.

choices.text: No: the question type changes from yes or no to why.
Yes: the meaning is kept and the tense moves back one step.
No: a condition has been left out of the original question by mistake.

feedback.es: Conserva el tipo de pregunta (sí o no) y retrocede el tiempo de did enjoy a had enjoyed: es fiel. No añade ni omite nada.

hint.es: Compara el tipo de pregunta, el contenido y el tiempo verbal entre el original y el informe.

origin.text: Leo is interviewed for a place at a language school. The interviewer asks him: «Did you enjoy the course?» Later, Leo tells his sister: «They asked me whether I had enjoyed the course.»

prompt.es: ¿Qué defecto tiene este informe del día de la entrevista?

choices.text: It omits the date mentioned by the manager.
It changes the person who asked the question.
It exaggerates: a question becomes a demand.

feedback.es: La pregunta «Can you start…?» se convierte en una exigencia con enfado añadido: el informe exagera el grado.

hint.es: Mira el verbo de reporte: ¿una pregunta es lo mismo que una exigencia?

origin.text: Original question from the manager: «Can you start in June?» Report that Carlos gave to his friends: «The manager demanded that I start in June, and he was not happy about it.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preguntaron si podía empezar en junio.»

feedback.es: En el informe can retrocede un paso a could; la pregunta de sí o no se mantiene con if.

hint.es: Es la forma pasada de can.

origin.text: The manager had asked Leo, «Can you start in June?» That evening Leo told his father, «They asked me if I ___ start in June.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué defecto tiene el primer informe de Sam.

choices.text: It changes the question: yes or no becomes why.
It makes the question sound like an order.
It matches what the interviewer really asked.

feedback.es: La pregunta original era de sí o no y Sam la cuenta como una pregunta con why: cambia su tipo y, con él, su sentido.

origin.audio: Sam's interview lasted twenty minutes. At the start, the interviewer looked at him and asked: can you start next week? Later that evening, Sam told his father that the interviewer had asked him why he wanted to start next week. Then he said that she had demanded that he finish his degree before September, although in fact she had only asked whether he thought he could manage both. His father sighed and said that Sam's version did not sound like the same interview.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué defecto tiene el segundo informe de Sam sobre sus estudios?

choices.text: It changes a yes-or-no question into a why-question.
It turns a cautious question into a demand.
It makes the question sound easier than it was.

feedback.es: La entrevistadora solo preguntó si podría con ambas cosas; Sam dice que exigió terminar antes de septiembre. Convierte una pregunta prudente en una exigencia; el cambio a why es del primer informe.

origin.audio: Sam's interview lasted twenty minutes. At the start, the interviewer looked at him and asked: can you start next week? Later that evening, Sam told his father that the interviewer had asked him why he wanted to start next week. Then he said that she had demanded that he finish his degree before September, although in fact she had only asked whether he thought he could manage both. His father sighed and said that Sam's version did not sound like the same interview.

prompt.es: Original: «¿Puedes trabajar los fines de semana?» Valora cada informe.

pairs: They demanded that I work at weekends.

pairs.es: Exagera: una pregunta pasa a exigencia

pairs: They asked whether I could work.

pairs.es: Omite un dato: los fines de semana

pairs: They asked why I work at weekends.
They asked whether I could work at weekends.

feedback.es: Cada informe falla de una manera distinta: exagera el grado, omite un dato o cambia el tipo de pregunta; solo uno conserva todo.

pairs: They demanded that I work at weekends.

pairs.es: Exagera: una pregunta pasa a exigencia

pairs: They asked whether I could work.

pairs.es: Omite un dato: los fines de semana

prompt.es: Escucha y decide qué defecto tiene el informe de la candidata.

choices.text: It changes the question from yes or no to why.
It exaggerates how much the panel wanted Saturdays.
It leaves out the condition about the mornings.

feedback.es: El informe conserva la pregunta de sí o no y su tiempo verbal, pero omite la condición («only in the mornings»), que cambia lo que se pregunta.

origin.audio: The panel asked whether she could work on Saturdays, but only in the mornings, because the afternoons were already full. When her friend asked her about the interview, she said: they asked me if I could work on Saturdays. Her friend nodded, but the panel would hardly have recognised that version of its own question.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hace este informe con el tono del original?

choices.text: It turns a neutral invitation into criticism and an order.
It faithfully passes on a polite suggestion made by the interviewer.
It leaves out the subject of the original question.

feedback.es: El original es una invitación neutra; el informe la convierte en reproche («lacked») y obligación («must»): distorsiona el tono.

origin.text: Interviewer: «You haven't mentioned any experience abroad. Is that something you would like to develop?» Candidate's later report to a friend: «He told me that I lacked experience abroad and that I must develop it.»

prompt.es: Completa: «El informe no copió las palabras, pero fue totalmente fiel a su sentido.»

feedback.es: Be faithful to + nombre: mantenerse fiel al sentido; un informe puede cambiar las palabras y seguir siendo fiel.

origin.text: The report did not copy a single word of the question, yet it was completely ___ to its meaning, so the panel would have recognised it at once.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me preguntaron cuánto tiempo había vivido en el extranjero.»

answer.text: They asked me how long I had lived abroad

feedback.es: How long + had lived: la pregunta «How long have you lived abroad?» retrocede al pasado perfecto y mantiene el orden afirmativo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué ha perdido este informe respecto a la pregunta original?

choices.text: The tense: the original was in the past, so the report should use had.
The reason: a why-question became a yes-or-no question.
A condition: the original added a limit that the report omitted.

feedback.es: La pregunta pedía un motivo (why); el informe la reduce a sí o no y pierde justo lo que el comité quería saber.

origin.text: Original: «Why are you interested in this school?» Report: «They asked me if I was interested in the school.» Ana, who had been in the room, said that the report sounded polite but had lost something important.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ilustra esta historia.

choices.text: How panels often suspect candidates of lying about their experience.
How references are usually checked before interviews.
How retelling can turn a neutral question into blame.

feedback.es: La petición rutinaria de una referencia se convirtió en un cargo grave al contarla: la historia muestra cómo el relato distorsiona una pregunta neutra.

origin.audio: When my sister described her interview, she said the panel had practically accused her of lying about her experience. But when I read the notes she had sent me afterwards, the question was simply whether she could provide a reference for that job. Somewhere between the room and the retelling, a routine request had been turned into a serious charge.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si omites la condición, el informe ya no será preciso.»

feedback.es: Omit the condition: dejar fuera un dato relevante; aunque la frase suene razonable, deja de ser un relato exacto.

origin.text: If you ___ the condition from the original question, your report will sound reasonable, but it will no longer be an accurate account of what was asked.
